Chapter 9: Practical Steps Toward Equity
Building a more equitable society can honestly feel overwhelming, can’t it? The problems seem huge, the history runs deep, and the obstacles are everywhere. But here’s the thing—every journey starts with a single step. And every step, no matter how small, really does matter.
The path to equity isn’t about big, dramatic gestures. It’s about the choices we make every single day. Small actions that, over time, start to add up.
Imagine this: there’s a city council member who’s frustrated because change feels so slow. She decides to focus on just one thing—making public transportation easier for everyone. So, she listens to riders, digs into the data, and pushes for new routes and lower fares. The process is slow, and there are plenty of setbacks. But as time goes on, more people can get to work, get to school, or reach their doctor’s appointments. The city becomes just a little more connected—and a little more fair.
Or think about a group of parents in a neighborhood. They notice that some kids are falling behind in school, so they start a tutoring program. They don’t have a lot of money or experience, but they do have determination. Week after week, they show up—helping with homework, encouraging the kids, and building trust. The progress isn’t instant, but after a while, you can see those kids starting to thrive.
Most practical steps toward equity are almost invisible. They don’t make the news or win awards. But that doesn’t mean they don’t matter. Every time someone challenges an unfair policy, every time a company hires a more diverse team, every time a teacher believes in a student who’s been written off—the world changes, even if it’s just a little.
A lot of people don’t realize just how much power they actually have to make a difference. It’s easy to believe that only experts or leaders can create real change. But the truth? Every act of fairness counts. Every moment we choose to include someone, every effort to listen and really understand—these are the building blocks of a more equitable world.
Here’s something worth remembering: the work of equity isn’t about getting everything perfect. It’s about sticking with it. There will be mistakes, setbacks, and days when it all feels impossible. But every effort counts. The journey is long, but it’s also full of moments that bring joy, connection, and hope.
In the end, the story of equity is written by people who just refuse to give up. When we take practical steps—no matter how small—we help build a society where everyone has a chance to belong.
